name: Northern Najdi Arabic (Shamali)

allophone_rules.notes: Northern Najdi extends the VOICELESS velar affrication to the central vowels, which Central Najdi does not. Alshammari (2026, JLTR 17(4):1333-1341, p.1335): /k/ is realized as [ts] "in the contiguity of the front short vowel /i/ and its long counterpart /i:/, and the central vowel /a/ and its long counterpart /a:/", with word-initial examples in ex. (1) /kalb/ -> [tsalb] \u0027dog\u0027, /kabd/ -> [tsabd] \u0027liver\u0027, /ka:.jid/ -> [tsa:.jid]. Formally the trigger is [-back]: p.1335 groups front and central vowels as [-back] coronal segments against the [+back] dorsal velar, and the OT constraint at pp.1338-1339 is *k<->[-back]. OPTIONAL: p.1335, "the process of affrication almost always remains optional in NNA ... [k] and [ts] are assumed to be in free variation". The author hedges the central trigger to "in certain cases" (p.1337) and records that a word-medial central-/a/ affrication was hard to attest (p.1336); the rule is stated whole here as he generalises it, and that choice is deliberate rather than silent. This rule ADDS to the inherited NAJD_AFFRIC_K_BEFORE rather than replacing it, so the resolved environment is the union of front and central.

The word-final half of SHAMALI_AFFRIC_K_BEFORE_CENTRAL. Alshammari (2026) p.1336 attests /k/ adjacent to central /a/ word-finally while noting that a word-final example next to /a:/ was difficult to find. Same optionality and same [-back] trigger.

notes:
Northern Najdi (Shamali) of Haʾil, the variety of Alshammari (2026), spoken across the northern Najd. IT DIFFERS FROM ITS PARENT IN EXACTLY ONE RULE and the spec carries only that rule; everything else -- qaf as /ɡ/, the interdentals, gahawa, emphasis spreading, stress -- is inherited from ar-SA-x-najd unchanged.

THE DELTA. Central Najdi affricates /k/ -> [ts] next to front vowels only. Northern Najdi extends it to the central vowels /a a:/ as well, so /kalb/ 'dog' is [tsalb] here and [kalb] in the parent. The VOICED counterpart is NOT extended: /ɡ/ -> [dz] stays restricted to /i i:/ in both, which Alshammari states as a phonological asymmetry (p.1337) and the parent already encodes. The two rules were always separate in this repo, which is why widening one does not touch the other -- an earlier ruling that a Shamali spec was impossible assumed that widening /k/ would force qaf-initial /ɡalb/ 'heart' to *[dzalb], and it does not, because that word is reached by the /ɡ/ rule.

WHAT IS NOT MODELLED, AND WHY. Loanwords resist affrication even where the environment is met: Alshammari ex. (4) p.1336 gives /ka.latʃ/ 'clutch', /tað.ki.rah/ 'ticket', /ka.bat/ 'cupboard' and /mi.ki:.nah/ 'machine' as unaffricated "because these words have been borrowed from either Modern Standard Arabic or other languages". That is a lexical stratum, not a phonological environment, so it belongs in word_exceptions rather than in the rule. No word_exceptions are written here because the source gives the forms in IPA and not in Arabic orthography, and constructing the spellings would be a guess; a future editor with the orthographic forms should add them, and until then the rule over-applies on MSA and foreign vocabulary.

POSITIONAL ATTESTATION IS UNEVEN and the author says so: p.1336 records that a word-medial affrication next to central /a/ was difficult to find, and likewise a word-final one next to /a:/. His own summary at p.1337 therefore reads "in certain cases". This spec follows his generalisation over front and central vowels rather than scoping to the attested positions, which is the less conservative of the two readings and is recorded here so the choice is visible.

NO WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE DESCRIBES THIS VARIETY ON ITS OWN. The `wikipedia` field carries the Najdi Arabic articles, which treat Northern Najdi as one of the sub-dialects; they are the parent's references and are listed here because the field is required, not because either article describes the delta modelled above.
